basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 11.' and it opens 'Vers. 11. Nunc igitur maledictus eris super terram quae aperuit os suum. In'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 11. Nunc igitur maledictus eris super terram quae aperuit os suum. In praevaricatione Adae, sicut | jam diximus, terra maledicta est, non ipse. In peccato autem Cain ipse maledicitur, quia sciens reatum primae praevaricationis non timuit, sed insuper scelus homicidii vel fratricidii adjecit. Allegorice superius diximus Cain Judaeos significare, Abel Christum. Terra vero hoc loco Ecclesiam significat, quae fusum Christi sanguinem aperto ore, id est magnae devotionis desiderio, ad aeternam suscipit salutem
